The seed Mockingjay remains the best design, but it leaves significant headroom on several traces. On 627.cam4_s-573B, which has 52.4% headroom, the largest mistake is should_bypass, meaning the policy inserts lines that are never reused. You can address this by changing the decision logic to bypass fills when the policy remembers that similar lines historically saw no reuse. Conversely, on 605.mcf_s-1644B, 619.lbm_s-2677B, 459.GemsFDTD-1491B, and 433.milc-127B, the largest mistake is wrong_bypass, where lines are bypassed but reused before resident lines. To fix this, the policy must remember when bypassed lines are prematurely requested and adjust its insertion decisions to keep them in the cache. Additionally, on 657.xz_s-2302B, the primary mistake is kept_dead, requiring the policy to remember long-term reuse patterns to evict dead lines sooner. To achieve these better decisions, you could declare a new word to express a dynamic bypass threshold or a specialized confidence counter that tracks the success rate of recent bypass decisions, which the existing vocabulary cannot currently express.
